entry.title: [UPDATED] GHSA-rjwr-m7qx-3fjr: oapi-codegen: OpenAPI Server Description Escapes Generated Go Comment and Injects Executable Code

oapi-codegen: OpenAPI Server Description Escapes Generated Go Comment and Injects Executable Code

Aliases: GO-2026-6016

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:N

Affected:

  • github.com/oapi-codegen/oapi-codegen/v2 — fixed in 2.7.1

## Summary The vulnerability in oapi-codegen seems to be similar with CVE-2026-22785, which is a generated-code injection issue where untrusted OpenAPI `summary` text is embedded into generated TypeScript MCP server source without proper escaping. `oapi-codegen` has a similar vulnerability in its server URL generator: untrusted OpenAPI `servers[].description` text is inserted into a generated Go line comment without normalizing embedded newlines. A crafted description can break out of the comment, add imports through `goimports`, and emit executable Go declarations into the generated package. > [!NOTE] > A vulnerability like this requires that it is missed in code review **and** that you then call the malicious method. > > Using an `init()` function could be enough to not require a dir…

entry.title: [NEW] GHSA-rhj7-vh3v-mcq6: Daptin: ParseAcceptLanguage `_` separator bypass enables >250x CPU amplification via Accept-Language header in LanguageMiddleware
entry.content:
Daptin: ParseAcceptLanguage `_` separator bypass enables >250x CPU amplification via Accept-Language header in LanguageMiddleware

Aliases: CVE-2026-62160

Severity: CVSS_V4: CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:N/PR:N/UI:N/VC:N/VI:N/VA:H/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N

Affected:

  • github.com/daptin/daptin

### Summary Daptin's `LanguageMiddleware` (registered as a global gin middleware) calls `golang.org/x/text/language.ParseAcceptLanguage` on the raw `Accept-Language` header of every HTTP request without imposing any size or shape filter. The underlying parser has quadratic-time behaviour on long lists of malformed language tags. The CVE-2022-32149 guard that golang.org/x/text added in v0.3.8 caps the number of `-` characters in the input at 1000, but it does not cap `_` characters even though the parser's internal scanner aliases `_` to `-` before parsing. A single unauthenticated GET request with an `Accept-Language` header built out of `_` separators (only 256 KiB, not even the 1 MiB ceiling) consumes about 27 seconds of server CPU on the host running Daptin. A 1 MiB payload exceeds the…

entry.title: [NEW] GHSA-8rvj-mm4h-c258: cert-manager: Direct ACME Challenge resources can bypass Issuer DNS01 solver policy and use ClusterIssuer DNS credentials
entry.content:
cert-manager: Direct ACME Challenge resources can bypass Issuer DNS01 solver policy and use ClusterIssuer DNS credentials

Aliases: BIT-cert-manager-2026-62290, CVE-2026-62290

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:L/A:N

Affected:

  • github.com/cert-manager/cert-manager — fixed in 1.19.6
  • github.com/cert-manager/cert-manager — fixed in 1.20.3

## Summary `Challenge` resources under `acme.cert-manager.io` can be created directly by namespace users. On create, cert-manager performs no admission validation tying the Challenge to an `Order`, an owner reference, or an Issuer-selected solver. The ACME Challenge controller then reconciles the direct resource and uses `Challenge.spec.solver` as the DNS01 provider configuration. When the direct Challenge references a `ClusterIssuer`, cert-manager derives the DNS provider secret namespace and ambient-credential policy from the `ClusterIssuer` reference, but the DNS provider configuration itself is attacker-controlled through `Challenge.spec.solver`. This lets a namespace user bypass `Issuer`/`ClusterIssuer` solver selectors such as `dnsZones`, `dnsNames`, and `matchLabels`, and make the…

entry.title: [UPDATED] GO-2026-6809: Distrust compromised intermediate certificates in crypto/x509
entry.content:
Distrust compromised intermediate certificates in crypto/x509

Aliases: BIT-golang-2026-111943, CVE-2026-111943, RUSTSEC-2026-0381, RUSTSEC-2026-0382, RUSTSEC-2026-0383

Affected:

  • stdlib — fixed in 1.26.10, 1.27.3

On most platforms, Go uses the given system root certificates. However, in some narrower cases, the system trust stores may not be updated without further action. To defend against the narrower set of cases that may remain affected, a denylist was added in crypto/x509 to return an error when calling Verify with any of the known intermediate certificates that are no longer considered to be trustworthy.

entry.title: [NEW] GHSA-v753-g4cw-jm48: Echo has Open Redirect via Control-Character Prefix Defeating sanitizeURI
entry.content:
Echo has Open Redirect via Control-Character Prefix Defeating sanitizeURI

Aliases: CVE-2026-118656

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:R/S:C/C:L/I:L/A:N

Affected:

  • github.com/labstack/echo/v5 — fixed in 5.4.0
  • github.com/labstack/echo/v4 — fixed in 4.16.0

## Summary Echo's dedicated open-redirect guard, `sanitizeURI`, decides whether a redirect target is a local path by inspecting exactly two byte positions: `uri[0]` and `uri[1]`. If the value begins with a control character such as a tab or a newline, followed by a separator pair, the guard does not fire and the value is written to the `Location` header unchanged. Browsers remove tab and newline characters from URLs before parsing them, and treat a backslash as a forward slash for HTTP and HTTPS URLs. A `Location` value of ``/\t/attacker.example`` is therefore resolved by the browser as an absolute URL on `attacker.example`. Confirmed end to end in a headless browser. ## Technical background ### The guard `middleware/slash.go:144` (duplicated verbatim at `echo.go:958`): ```go func sa…

entry.title: [NEW] GHSA-3pmx-cf9f-34xr: Echo static file middleware route protection bypass via encoded dot-dot traversal
entry.content:
Echo static file middleware route protection bypass via encoded dot-dot traversal

Aliases: CVE-2026-118654

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:N/A:N

Affected:

  • github.com/labstack/echo/v5 — fixed in 5.4.0
  • github.com/labstack/echo/v4 — fixed in 4.16.0

## Summary Echo v5.2.0 contains a bypass of the fix for GHSA-vfp3-v2gw-7wfq. The fix rejects encoded path separators such as `%2F` and `%5C` before static file path unescaping, but two traversal forms still bypass route-level middleware protections for static files. The primary bypass uses encoded dot-dot segments. A request such as `/public/%2E%2E/admin/secret.txt` passes the encoded-separator guard, is unescaped to `public/../admin/secret.txt`, then `path.Clean` resolves it to `admin/secret.txt`. If `/admin/*` is protected by middleware but the static filesystem is mounted at `/`, the protected file is returned through the public static route. A second bypass exists when `UseEscapedPathForMatching=true`. In that mode, the router normalizes encoded separators before the static handler …

## Summary Commit a9ede66a (PR #3006, issue #2599) silently fixed a path traversal vulnerability in the Echo web framework's static file middleware. ## Vulnerability The static middleware double-unescaped URL paths. entry.title: [NEW] GHSA-23wf-92cp-8pcj: Echo has Arbitrary Scheme Injection in WWWRedirect/NonWWWRedirect Middlewares via X-Forwarded-Proto

Echo has Arbitrary Scheme Injection in WWWRedirect/NonWWWRedirect Middlewares via X-Forwarded-Proto

## Summary The `c.Scheme()` method in Echo (`context.go:162-181`) trusts the `X-Forwarded-Proto`, `X-Forwarded-Protocol`, and `X-Url-Scheme` request headers without validating that the value is `http` or `https`. Echo's middleware.Static: `%2F`-encoded path bypasses route/group middleware guarding a statically-served path

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:N/A:N

Affected:

## Summary When `middleware.Static` is mounted globally (`e.Use(middleware.Static(...))`) and an application relies on a **route- or group-level middleware guard** to restrict a path that also falls under the served static root, a `%2F`-encoded request bypasses that guard while the file is still served. This is the same encoding/decoding mismatch fixed for `StaticFS`/`StaticDirectoryHandler` in CVE-2026-55677 / GHSA-vfp3-v2gw-7wfq, but the fix did not cover the `middleware.Static` path. In addition, the `StaticConfig.EnablePathUnescaping` docstring states the default configuration prevents exactly this bypass, which is inaccurate for the global-mount case. **This is not path traversal:** no file outside the static root is accessed. The served file lives inside the static root; the issue …
